items.headline: Google-Linked $3 Billion Prepaid Bond Sales Postponed on Market Volatility / Alphabet-Linked Municipal Bond Demand Cools; $3 Billion Prepaid Energy Deal Pricing Postponed
items.claim: FourWeekMBA (19 Nov, relaying Bloomberg): two prepaid energy deals totalling USD 3bn, issued through the Southeast Energy Authority with Alphabet as funding recipient and Arizona's Salt River Project as utility, Goldman Sachs managing both, preliminary documents posted 16 Nov, were delayed on 'lackluster investor demand amid market volatility'; municipal bonds underperformed and cheapened against Treasuries this week; no new date, revised size or yield levels; Alphabet's 2026 prepaid energy bonds via the California Community Choice Financing Authority total ~USD 5.85bn (1.2bn priced 4 Jun on >10bn of orders; 1.65bn priced 4 Nov, oversubscribed from >80 accounts; 3bn delayed) - the delayed piece is ~51% of the year's total; Sage Advisory warned in June that spreads on Alphabet-backed prepaids 'could widen by 25 to 50 basis points'. Longbridge/Zhitong (19 Nov 23:46Z): sluggish demand amid volatility; a source says the transactions are 'still proceeding'; Goldman and Google declined to comment; Columbia Threadneedle's Shannon Rinehart: 'the spreads some investors ultimately want do not align with the levels the issuer is willing to offer'; Allspring's Andy Hobbs: large prepaid transactions are more sensitive to volatility, expects relaunch 'soon after the holidays' with relatively strong demand; in the 4 Nov deal the 2039 tranche's initial guidance was 5.15% (~138bp over AAA) and the 2040 tranche priced at 111bp; GOOGL -3.46%, GOOG -2.93%.

items.note: Hard-event test (pulled or downsized hyperscaler/registered-ticker deal) NOT strictly met: the deals are postponed with no stated size cut and the underwriter says they are proceeding. Recorded as the nearest reading to date because the cause is demand/spread, not regulation, the obligor is a registered ticker (GOOGL) and it lands the same day as the sixth straight S&P loss and a 2% rout. Structure is a tax-exempt prepaid energy bond where Alphabet's credit backs the utility's prepayment - muni-market channel, not corporate IG. Watch for relaunch size/spread.

items.name: Update vs 11-19: Anthropic 'ANT' Nasdaq debut Thu 19 Nov - first trade 11:48 ET at USD 111.50 (+34% vs 83 IPO), high 114.99, low 92.72, close 97.17 (+17.07%), ~USD 1.76-1.8tn fully diluted at the close vs ~2tn at the open; USD 81.3bn raised (largest IPO on record) plus USD 26bn conditional purchases by Google, Nvidia, Broadcom, Microsoft and others at the IPO price; after hours -4.70% to 92.60 (below the day low), reportedly on Apple AI-agent plans; pre-market Fri -6 to -8% per CNBC/World Today headlines; settlement Fri 20 Nov, 180-day lock-ups, no sell-side ratings until mid-December
items.headline: Anthropic (ANT) Stock $97.17: Day Two After a 17% Debut / Stocks Close Lower on the Day Anthropic Begins Trading / Anthropic shares fall 8% in premarket amid AI selloff as Nvidia, AMD shares drop
items.claim: stocktitan (19 Nov): IPO price USD 83 (range 70-78 set 17 Nov); opened 11:48 ET at 111.50, ~34% above; intraday high 114.99, low 92.72; close 97.17, ~17% above the IPO price; -1.50% after hours at 18:03 ET; 980m shares, ~USD 81.34bn; ~USD 2tn fully diluted at the opening price (CNBC); separate purchases of USD 26.0bn by Google, Nvidia, Broadcom, Microsoft and others at the IPO price, subject to conditions; settlement Fri 20 Nov; CNBC said investors appeared to take profits. cappnotes: ANT opened 111.50, closed 97.17 (+17.07%), raised USD 81.3bn, ended with ~USD 1.8tn fully diluted; AI shares reversed early gains into a broad afternoon sell-off. financefeeds (20 Nov 07:00Z): fell 4.70% to 92.60 after hours (Benzinga), below Thursday's 92.72 low; CNN 1.76tn / CNBC ~1.8tn / Yahoo 1.27tn fully diluted on different bases; most pre-IPO holders locked up 180 days, longer for co-founders and largest holders, some employee shares saleable earlier; 30-day over-allotment option; research begins after the 25-day quiet period (mid-December); El-Erian: the Nasdaq dip during Anthropic's surge was 'about making room for it'. Headlines (not fetched): Bloomberg 20 Nov 'Anthropic shares drop post-market on Apple's AI agent plans'; CNBC 20 Nov 'Anthropic shares fall 8% in premarket amid AI selloff'; World Today Journal 'drop 6% premarket as tech rout intensifies'. Saxo: gains faded after a stronger opening.

items.note: Extends the 11-19 Japan-tranche item: pricing and tranche detail were recorded yesterday; new today is the trading outcome. The deal cleared (not pulled, not downsized) - what reads as an event is the liquidity-drain pattern: Nasdaq swung from +2% to -2.25% around the first print, and Asia sold AI chains 5-6% the next morning. Day-two trading is after run time; the -6/-8% pre-market figures are headlines not verified by fetch.
